_comment: FITTED CONSTANTS FOR THIS PHYSICAL ROBOT — calibration data, not defaults.
They lived on the systemd unit's ExecStart, which the BOM doc (§9.2, §3.3) flags as
the wrong home twice over: a value invisible to anyone reading the docs, and one that
the checked-in unit did not carry, so reinstalling it silently dropped the ToF
calibration. Both now live here, the way servo_map.json and poses.json already do,
so they travel with the robot and BOTH programs read the same number.
CLI flags still override, for bench work.

tof._why: The sensor rides a SOLID BOOM off one of the HAT's mounting screws, ~4 mm below the top of the HAT, looking down (BOM §9.1 'as built'; it cannot go inside the chassis because the battery is there). Sitting high puts the belly's 0-56 mm working range above the part's unreliable short end. Anchored at BELLY-DOWN, which folds the part's own 8-11 mm long-reading bias into the offset and puts the calibration at the dangerous end of the channel. Re-fit after any belly re-assembly. ⚠ An earlier version of this note said the sensor was 'recessed up inside the chassis', which described a mount that has never existed on this robot -- the number was right and its stated reason was wrong. ⚠ RE-READ 2026-09-26 against the X pose: belly-down measures 68.0 mm (sd 1.97, n=76), so this 64.8 is 3.2 mm PERMISSIVE and clearance reads +0.0032 m with the belly flat on the floor. Deliberately NOT re-fitted from that sample -- see BOM §9.9.

ina219._why: At 10 mOhm the trace and solder resistance are a material fraction of the shunt, so this is a fitted value rather than the part's nominal. Raw counts are what get recorded; this only derives amps, so a re-fit can re-derive already-captured samples.

ground_clearance._why: The normalizer the promoted height homeostat rides: published signal = clamp(raw_m / stand_m, 0, 1). MUST match the sim's GROUND_CLEARANCE_STAND or the robot feeds a differently-scaled number into a promoted lever. Shared implementation: ogma::body::ground_clearance().

imu._why: Chip-frame body-up with the belly flat on a level floor (BOM §4.2: five placements over four verified 180° rotations, 0.05° repeatability, floor slope 0.49° subtracted out). It lumps mount tilt together with accelerometer bias, unsplit, and is applied to the ACCELEROMETER ONLY. Icm20948Config's default carries the same 2026-09-10 fit and its comment asked for exactly this file; re-fit after any IMU remount.

servo._why: MEASURED, not the datasheet default. Command a known us delta and measure the toe's swept chord against the known tibia radius L3=76.5 mm: angle = 2*asin(chord/2L3). Seven marks at 100 us steps, PWM held through each mark by a 5 Hz keepalive. ⚠ THE KEEPALIVE IS NOT OPTIONAL: benchd's deadman (DEADMAN_MS=1000) commands the saved RESCUE POSE when no client command is fresh — this HAT cannot limp a servo at all, so 'safe' is a pose, not slack. A rescue excursion of only 100-200 us looks like nothing happening and silently replaces the commanded angle with rescue's. Gap-average 549.0 and the 700->1300 chord 545.2 agree to 0.7%; chord/arc 0.958 against a predicted 0.950 confirms a true 76.5 mm arc — which also retroactively proves the femur did not wander between marks, since it could not otherwise. INDEPENDENT CHECK: at this scale the calibrated knee envelope 600-2300 us spans 178.6 deg, a hobby servo's full mechanical travel; at the standard 636.6 us/rad it would be 153 deg, leaving 27 deg unexplained.
servo._caveat: One channel (RL knee). Part-to-part scale should hold within a few percent — the per-channel origin_us differences in servo_map.json are horn mounting, not scale — but this has not been checked on a second joint. The 600->700 gap was discarded: it starts from a position the deadman had already pulled to rescue, so its true angle is not the commanded one, and it was the clear outlier (449 vs 509-588 us/rad).
